name: Russian Federation

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 17,125,190 km2; low is land area 16,376,870 km2. Internationally recognised territory; occupied Ukrainian territory (Crimea and parts of four oblasts, ~100,000+ km2) not included.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank 143,513,328, declining ~0.1%/yr). High allows for Russian official statistics that include annexed Crimea (a few million higher; not fetched). Population of occupied Ukrainian territories excluded.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.188 as quoted: 1,264,000 active (plus 569,000 paramilitary, excluded). CIA Factbook 2025: 1.1-1.2 million (low); September 2024 decree sets 1.5 million servicemen (high, a target). Wartime: high casualties (~1 million killed and wounded by mid-2025 per the Russian Armed Forces article, Western estimates) are replaced by contract recruitment.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 1,500,000 reserves (mid). Low is what was actually called up in the 2022 partial mobilization (~300,000, IISS Feb 2023 as quoted on the Russian Ground Forces article), i.e. the realistic 30-day intake. High: "close to two million" reservists (Russian Armed Forces article).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 1,264,000 minus infantry P roles (300,000 + 100,000). Aerospace Forces, Navy, Strategic Rocket Forces, crews, artillery, drone units (Unmanned Systems Forces), logistics, staff, and the ~20,000 deployed in other former Soviet states/Africa (CIA Factbook 2025).

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to the USSR in WWII (roughly 34 million mobilized from ~195 million, ~17%) scaled down for a smaller, older population, emigration since 2022 and a labour-short war economy. Ukrainian C-in-C Syrskyi (Apr 2025, a party to the war) claimed Russia could mobilize 20 million (14%), 5 million with military training (Russian Armed Forces article).

count.note: Educated guess. The grouping in Ukraine was ~623,000 in April 2025 and growing 8-9,000/month (Syrskyi, as quoted; CIA Factbook 2025: ~600,000 in Ukraine). The war is infantry-heavy (motor-rifle and "assault" units of contract soldiers and mobilized men); about half of the grouping taken as line infantry.

quality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: era-typical small arms and drones, but many units ride MT-LB/old BMPs or go on foot; a generation behind NATO in protection.

training.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: short training for contract recruits (weeks), offset by combat experience of survivors.

count.note: Educated guess. Airborne Forces (VDV), naval infantry, Spetsnaz, Storm-Z/Storm-V penal assault units, plus foreign contingents (North Korean troops deployed 2024-25 excluded).

training.note: Rubric 0.5: elite VDV/naval infantry cadres largely destroyed in 2022-23 and refilled; penal units 0.25.

count.note: Highly uncertain wartime figure. High: ~3,460 tanks in service per the new IISS Military Balance edition (as reported by www1.ru, May 2026; the same 3,460 appears on the Ground Forces equipment list: T-54/55 120, T-62 600, T-64 50, T-72 1,470, T-80 600, T-90M 620), with ~2,100 left in storage. Low: 1,750 active (IISS 2024, mind.ua). Losses since 2022 exceed 3,000 (IISS 2024).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: T-90M/T-80BVM/T-72B3M current, but a large share are refurbished T-62/T-55 (obsolete, 0.25).

count.note: IISS as quoted on the equipment list: IFVs 1,950 (BMP-1 750, BMP-2 550, BMP-3 650; IISS 2025) + APCs BTR-60 800, BTR-70 200, BTR-80 1,200, MT-LB 2,500 (IISS 2024) = ~6,650. BMD airborne vehicles not counted (high). Up to 3,000 BMP-1/2 and 1,000 MT-LB in storage excluded.

IISS 2025 as quoted: SP 1,675 (2S1 400, 2S3 600, 2S19 450, 2S5 100, 2S7 125) + towed 152mm 370 + D-30 200 + MLRS 1,181 = ~3,426 active. ~4,800 more in storage (SP 1,900, towed 152mm 1,650, MLRS 1,250) feed refurbishment (high). Artillery advantage over Ukraine fell from ~10:1 to ~2:1 by 2025 (Syrskyi, as quoted).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 era-typical; Tornado-S/2S19M2 modern, many barrels worn.

training.note: Rubric 0.5 plus combat experience in counter-battery and drone-spotted fires.

count.note: Active-aircraft list (World Air Forces 2025 / IISS 2022 as quoted): Su-27/30/35 combined "<422", naval Su-30SM 22, Su-57 29, MiG-29 ~87, MiG-31 128+ and 32 naval, MiG-35 6 = ~726; list subtotal ~1,069 double-counts across tables (high).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: Su-35S/Su-30SM2 modern 4+ generation, only ~29 Su-57.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: low peacetime flying hours, but extensive stand-off combat sorties since 2022.

count.note: World Air Forces 2025 as quoted: Su-24 259, Su-25 175, Su-34 142-163, Tu-22M3 55, Tu-95MS 46, Tu-160 17 = ~700 (high). Mid discounts the Su-24 count (many retired/stored) and combat losses; Bulletin 2026: ~60 heavy bombers active.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Su-34 and glide bombs (UMPK) effective; Su-24/Su-25/Tu-95 old airframes.

count.note: World Air Forces 2025 as quoted: attack Ka-52 135 + Mi-28 94 + Mi-24 323 = 552; transport/utility Mi-8/17 777 + Mi-26 45 + Ka-226 36 + Ansat-U 50 = 908; total ~1,460 (high). Mid allows for war losses.

Educated guess. Reusable Group 2+ UAVs (Orlan-10/30, Zala, Supercam, Orion, Forpost) in service; no fetched inventory. FPV drones (millions per year) and one-way attack drones (Geran) are munitions and excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: mass-produced, combat-iterated designs; few large MALE drones.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: Unmanned Systems Forces formed from combat-experienced units (Rubikon).

count.note: Convention: carriers + cruisers + destroyers + frigates. Active list (statuses partly 2021-24): cruisers 2 + destroyers 6 + frigates 9-12 (mid 11) = 19; high adds the non-operational carrier Kuznetsov, battlecruiser Admiral Nakhimov on trials and damaged/refit hulls. Moskva and other Black Sea Fleet ships lost 2022-24.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Admiral Gorshkov frigates modern (Zircon), destroyers/cruisers 1980s.

count.note: Active list tallies: corvettes ~47 operational (8 large + ~39 small missile ships; page summary c. 79 incl. reserve), landing ships ~10-17, mine countermeasures 42+, patrol ships 5 (patrol boats excluded). Mid ~110.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Karakurt/Buyan-M corvettes carry Kalibr; old landing ships and MCM.

count.note: Active list: operational SSBN 12 + SSGN 4 + SSN 10 + SSK 16 = 42 (low); page summary incl. refit/reserve 57 (high). Bulletin Nuclear Notebook (Mar 2026): 13 operational SSBNs.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Yasen-M and Borei-A among era best; older Akula/Oscar/Kilo.

training.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: submarine force is the best-maintained navy branch.

count.note: Launchers: ~324 ICBMs (Yars ~207, Voevoda ~40, Topol-M, Avangard; Bulletin Nuclear Notebook Mar 2026) + 162 Iskander-M launchers (IISS 2025 as quoted on the equipment list) = ~486. High allows for Bastion/Bal coastal anti-ship launchers (not counted).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: Iskander-M, Kinzhal, Zircon, Oreshnik IRBM (used Nov 2024); Sarmat not on combat duty.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: Strategic Rocket Forces are well-trained long-service units.

count.note: Educated guess in batteries: Ground Forces SAM systems 1,029+ (Strela-10 300, Tunguska 190, Osa 100, Tor 129+, Buk 310; IISS 2025) / ~4 per battery = ~260, plus Aerospace Forces S-300/S-400/S-350 battalions (~80-120, not fetched). Several S-300/S-400 units destroyed in Crimea/occupied areas 2023-25.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: S-400, Pantsir-SM, Tor-M2 among era best; older Osa/Strela.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5 (competent staff, average generalship): failed 2022 opening, then effective defensive operations (2023) and slow attritional advances; centralized command, generals purged/killed; reportedly improving drone-artillery integration.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: national army but filled with pay-motivated contract volunteers, mobilized men, convicts and foreign recruits; units repeatedly reconstituted after losses; ~250,000+ draft evaders fled (Russian Armed Forces article).

morale.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: high signing bonuses rather than enthusiasm, heavy casualties; would rise toward 0.75 for defence of Russian territory proper.

weapons.note: Anchor 10 partly: hypersonic Kinzhal/Zircon, Oreshnik IRBM, glide bombs, mass drones; precision-munition stocks limited; much Soviet-era equipment.

armor.note: Anchor 9 composite/ERA armour; Arena-M APS fielded only in small numbers; field-improvised anti-drone cages.

ships.note: Anchor 9 (nuclear subs) with Yasen-M/Zircon toward 10; surface fleet aging, no networked USV fleet.

fortification.note: Anchor 10: layered air defence (S-400, Pantsir), deep fortified lines in occupied Ukraine (2023 "Surovikin line").

logistics.note: Between anchor 8 (motor transport + rail) and 9: rail-dependent, truck-poor (forces operate ~90 miles from railheads, War on the Rocks 2021); limited airlift.

communications.note: Anchor 9 satellite comms and data links, but chronic shortages of secure tactical radios (use of commercial phones/Starlink terminals reported 2022-24).

isr.note: Anchor 9-10: dense tactical drone ISR, limited satellite and AEW (few A-50 left).

air.note: Anchor 9-10: Su-35/Su-34 4+ generation; Su-57 5th generation in small numbers only.

cyber.note: Anchor 10 state cyber forces: GRU units (Sandworm etc.), FSB, SVR.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD 42,358.0 (2021 int$) x 0.8005 = 33,908 2011 int$. Range +/-15%.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 6,183,071,354,160 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 4,949,548,619,005 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 7.50% of GDP in 2025 (wartime, mid), 6.87% 2024, 3.60% 2021 (pre-war peacetime, low). The field is defined as peacetime share; mid is the current wartime value because the 2026 snapshot is at war. High allows for classified spending.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 29.7% of GDP; 32.2% in 2022.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: world's largest wheat exporter and self-sufficient in most staples; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 66,553,257 x share of males aged 15-19 6.260% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 833,199. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

armor.note: IISS (Military Balance 2024 as reported by swissinfo): Russia put ~1,000-1,500 tanks into service in a year, of which "200 at most were newly built"; the rest refurbished from storage (up to ~90/month). Low = new-build only: with ~2,100 left in storage (new IISS edition via www1.ru) refurbishment cannot continue at the mid rate beyond ~2027.

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess incl. refurbishment from storage (BMP-1/2, MT-LB); new-build BMP-3/BTR-82A a few hundred per year.

artillery.note: Educated guess incl. refurbished towed guns; barrel production is a known bottleneck.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess (Su-35S, Su-30SM2, Su-57 at Komsomolsk/Irkutsk).

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess (Su-34 at Novosibirsk; Tu-160M slow).

drones.note: Educated guess for reusable Group 2+ UAVs only. Excludes FPV drones and Geran-type one-way attack drones, which Western estimates put at tens of thousands per year (not fetched).

missiles.note: Educated guess for Iskander/Yars launchers per year; missile output itself is far higher.

roadKm.note: Rosstat 2023 as quoted: 1,124,116 km paved of 1,579,291 km total (high); only ~4,923 km expressway.

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 85,544 route-km (World Bank); CIA Factbook 85,494 km (2019). Broad (1,520 mm) gauge, differs from Europe and China (break of gauge at borders). Lines built into occupied Ukraine excluded.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 67 ports, 4 large + 5 medium = 9; key ports Arkhangelsk, De-Kastri, Dudinka, Kaliningrad, Murmansk, Novorossiysk, St Petersburg, Vladivostok, Vyborg. Separated across four fleets that cannot reinforce each other quickly.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 14,786 thousand DWT under the Russian flag. High is an educated guess adding the Russian-controlled "shadow fleet" of tankers under flags of convenience.

supplyRangeKm.note: War on the Rocks (Vershinin, 2021): Russian forces lack the trucks to sustain operations more than ~90 miles (145 km) beyond supply dumps/railheads; 180 miles (290 km) would need double the truck allocation (high). Borne out in 2022.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess for horses (not from FAO data). Militarily marginal, though some use of horses and donkeys by assault units was reported in 2025.

nuclearWarheads.note: Bulletin Nuclear Notebook (Mar 2026) and FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces (2026): military stockpile ~4,400 (1,796 deployed strategic, ~810 strategic in storage, ~1,794 nonstrategic, low confidence); total inventory incl. ~1,020 retired warheads 5,420 (high).

basesAbroad.name: Operational Group of Russian Forces, Tiraspol (Transnistria)
4th Military Base, Tskhinvali (South Ossetia, occupied Georgia)
Hmeimim Air Base, Syria (status uncertain after Dec 2024)
Tartus naval facility, Syria (status uncertain after Dec 2024)

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: deep strategic depth, harsh winter climate the invader is not adapted to, fortified cities and population support (the rubric names Russia as the example).

notes: WARTIME snapshot (4th year of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine), asOf 2025 economic data with a 2026 order of battle. All equipment counts are highly uncertain: IISS figures as quoted are from the 2023-2026 editions and mix active and refurbished stock; losses since 2022 exceed 3,000 tanks (IISS 2024) and the force is sustained by drawing down Soviet-era storage (~2,100 tanks left per the new IISS edition as reported May 2026). Population convention: internationally recognised territory inside ne:RUS (World Bank); occupied Crimea and parts of Ukraine, and their populations, excluded; forces deployed there are counted. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011 (+/-15%). ships_major = carriers + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = corvettes, landing ships, MCM, patrol ships; drones = reusable Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Rosgvardiya (~350,000) and other paramilitary (IISS 569,000) excluded. North Korean troops sent in 2024-25 excluded. Figures from Ukrainian officials (Syrskyi) are from a party to the war and used only as ranges.
